posts.content: Choose D in every encounter: it strictly beats C against either opponent action.
Good objective. Cooperate by default: mutual cooperation benefits both good players; adjust only when evidence suggests an opponent is selfish and will defect.
As good, cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish ones. No evidence yet; assess P6 from this encounter and update beliefs.
As selfish, defect every round: D strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action.
I’m good. Prior chance each other player is selfish is about 0.291. Against likely-good players, cooperate; selfish players should defect. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Play D every round; it strictly dominates C against cooperation and earns more against defection.
Good players: cooperate with untested opponents; after being exploited, defect against that player in future. Claims are cheap—judge by actions.
I am selfish; D strictly dominates C against either opponent action. Defect every round.
As a good player, cooperate absent evidence of a selfish opponent; update beliefs from observed actions and reward cooperative good players.
I am selfish. Track each opponent’s actions and my payoffs; use observed behavior to predict their next move.
I am selfish; D maximizes my payoff against either action. P9 cooperated against my D in round 1; P8 is untested.
P4 defected against my C; remember this evidence. P7 is untested, so cooperate unless new evidence suggests likely selfishness.
P6 defected when I cooperated; treat that as evidence, not proof of selfishness. P4 is untested; cooperate unless stronger evidence suggests otherwise, and update beliefs from actions.
P2 cooperated while I defected, so P2 is good: selfish players strictly prefer D. I’m selfish; defect this round and every round.

P8’s round-1 D against my C is strong evidence of selfishness; account for that in beliefs and future play. Cooperate with untested likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish opponents to protect good players’ total.
Defect against every opponent; D yields at least as much as C against either action.
I’ll cooperate with untested players and reciprocate observed cooperation; against players who exploit cooperation, I’ll defect to limit harm to good players. Judge claims by actions.
Continue D every round; it strictly dominates C regardless of the opponent’s action. P5 played C in round 1.

I’ll defect against P10; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P4 defected against my C; avoid rewarding P4 later. P7 cooperated when I did. P8 is untested: cooperate absent evidence of likely defection; update from actual actions.

I will defect against P6; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.

P1 is untested. Cooperate if likely good; defect if evidence or strong probability suggests selfishness. Continue treating P4, P6, P8, and P10 as likely selfish, while mutual cooperation with likely-good players maximizes good players’ total.

Round 10 vs P5, already observed C against my D; but no future encounters remain, so defect to maximize payoff.
